summary: Misión Umbral is a browser-based 2D mission trainer for children aged 7–12. Players choose suit upgrades, prepare a spacecraft and operate a fictional Mars habitat. With four batteries for six stations, they must prioritize life support, research, crops and communications. A NASA AVATAR-inspired activity introduces flight samples and Earth controls, while a shelter activity explores crew protection. The prototype includes keyboard and touch controls, short explanations, repeatable narration and local saving. It addresses the challenge “Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer” by turning planning and scientific observation into interactive decisions with visible consequences. The current game is in Spanish. Testing with children and evaluation of learning outcomes are planned.
details:
Misión Umbral responds to “Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer” with an interactive adventure about planning, resource management and scientific observation for children aged 7–12.

HOW IT WORKS

Players select three of six suit upgrades, compare their benefits and limitations, and prepare their spacecraft, cargo and shelter. Guided travel leads to a fictional Mars habitat.

Inside the habitat, players move an astronaut between four floors and carry batteries to six stations: air, water, heat, greenhouse, laboratory and communications. Only four batteries are available, so not every station can operate simultaneously. Players prioritize tasks, replenish their suit at service points, repair equipment, grow crops and respond to emergencies. Completing the initial Orion difficulty unlocks the harder Apollo option.

NASA SCIENCE

An activity inspired by NASA’s AVATAR investigation introduces flight samples and Earth controls. Players learn why scientific comparisons need a reference condition. The activity does not invent experimental results or diagnose an astronaut.

NASA resources about crew systems, spacesuits, communications and protection inform the explanations and equipment choices. The Mars habitat is fictional. Apollo and Orion are compared within the trainer, not presented as vehicles that transported crews to Mars. Resource values, equipment effects and event timing are educational gameplay rules, not engineering or medical predictions. No live NASA measurements or historical DONKI event dataset have been integrated.

CREATIVITY AND INTENDED IMPACT

The project connects preparation choices with later consequences. Players learn by moving, interacting, observing and trying another strategy. Our intended benefit is to make resource planning and scientific reasoning approachable through play. Learning outcomes have not yet been measured with children.

DEVELOPMENT AND ACCESS

The prototype uses Astro, React, TypeScript and CSS. It includes keyboard and touch controls, readable text, short explanations, repeatable browser narration, independent voice and music controls, pause, and local save/resume. No game account is required. Saves remain in the same browser.

The current public gameplay is in Spanish. AI-assisted translation of game text supports preparation of an English version. Further work includes testing with children, evaluating school and mobile devices, and refining difficulty.

TEAM AND AI ASSISTANCE

Angela Lopez and Samantha Urbano contributed creative proposals. Felipe and Jonny Agudelo worked on development.

AI tools assisted with checking and correcting errors, generating visual designs, developing and refining code, translating game text into English, and preparing the web version and shareable project link.
